definitions.explanation: Food cooked by steam. A healthy cooking method that preserves nutrients and natural flavors.

examples.japanese: {蒸|む}し{物|もの}は{油|あぶら}を{使|つか}わないのでヘルシーです。
examples.english: Steamed dishes are healthy because they don't use oil.

examples.japanese: {魚|さかな}の{蒸|む}し{物|もの}は{素材|そざい}の{味|あじ}が{活|い}きます。
examples.english: Steamed fish brings out the natural flavor of the ingredient.

examples.japanese: {蒸|む}し{物|もの}は{油|あぶら}を{使|つか}わないので、{体|からだ}にいい{料理|りょうり}だと{言|い}われています。
examples.english: Steamed dishes are said to be good for your health because they don't use oil.

examples.japanese: {竹|たけ}の{蒸籠|せいろ}を{使|つか}って{蒸|む}し{物|もの}を{作|つく}ると、{余分|よぶん}な{水分|すいぶん}を{吸|す}ってくれるので{仕上|しあ}がりがよくなります。
examples.english: When you use a bamboo steamer to make steamed dishes, it absorbs excess moisture and gives a better finish.

notes:
{蒸|む}し{物|もの} refers to steamed foods ({蒸|む}す = to steam).

Common Japanese steamed dishes:
- {茶碗蒸|ちゃわんむ}し (savory egg custard)
- {肉まん|にくまん} (steamed meat bun)
- {蒸|む}しパン (steamed bread)
- {酒蒸|さかむ}し (sake-steamed, e.g., clams)

Advantages of steaming:
- Preserves nutrients
- No added oil/fat
- Retains moisture and tenderness
- Brings out natural flavors

Equipment:
- {蒸籠|せいろ} (bamboo steamer)
- {蒸|む}し{器|き} (steamer)

Related cooking methods:
- {煮物|にもの} (simmered)
- {焼|や}き{物|もの} (grilled)
- {揚|あ}げ{物|もの} (fried)
